gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Binize's own store, selling the same '10 Inch Double Din Car Stereo with Wireless CarPlay Android Auto' (Android, 2 GB / 32 GB) that ChatGPT picked as cheapest, prices it at $129.99, not $89.99, and says its wiring harness 'comes standard and require[s] manual soldering' unless the buyer asks customer service for a plug-and-play harness before ordering.
standout_why: I compared against our own category page (dealectric.com/cheapest-10-inch-…, read 2026-11-14: no Binize, no Haudio, no soldering note, no Walmart vs maker-store comparison, no Samsung exclusion), the HowToGeek budget-head-unit article (names only a 7-inch Kissound at $85 and an unbranded $100 unit, gives no 10-inch prices and no harness or soldering detail) and pricehistory.app's Haudio page (price history only). ChatGPT's answers repeated Walmart marketplace prices for Binize ($89.99), Haudio ($71.99/$87.99) and ATOTO ($149.59), with nothing on installation cost or the maker's own price. The technobezz Kissound page and the Walmart and eBay pages returned 403 or a bot wall, so I could not check those.
decides: This partly overturns ChatGPT's 'cheapest' pick. Binize, the brand ChatGPT recommended most, says on its own store that the standard harness needs soldering. That is extra cost and work that the $89.99 Walmart figure hides, and Binize's own price for what looks like the same unit is $129.99. Binize's other 10-inch Android 12 universal units list 1024×600 screens and say CarPlay/Android Auto works 'not for Samsung'. Among brand-store prices I read today, the cheapest 10-inch units are an ESSGOO AR1001 'MP5' at $111.99 (wireless CarPlay/AA not confirmed) and Binize at $129.99 (needs soldering). ATOTO's cheapest 10-inch Android unit on its own store is $194.90 (with backup camera), and our Eonon UA13 Plus is $229.99 (1280×720, wireless both, 2-year warranty). The page should present the sub-$100 Walmart and Amazon listings as marketplace prices that need a harness check, not as the maker's price.
